story.title: U.S. and Iran Extend Pause on Attacks Amid Ceasefire Negotiations
story.summary: The United States and Iran have paused attacks for a second consecutive day as both sides aim to resume negotiations for an interim ceasefire. This development follows a period of heightened tensions and exchanges of fire, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz. The reasons behind the U.S. decision to halt its strikes remain unclear.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers chosen developments on July 22-23, 2026—including military threats, U.S. war-powers action and oil-market effects—and does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict, diplomacy, or humanitarian consequences.

explore_lenses.label: Why did both sides pause their attacks?
explore_lenses.title: A reciprocal lull, not a settled ceasefire
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate halt appears reciprocal: Washington stopped strikes after 13 consecutive nights, and Iran says it then suspended retaliatory operations. U.S. officials frame the move as space for diplomacy, while Iran frames its actions as retaliation rather than a unilateral ceasefire commitment.

claims.text: The U.S. pause followed 13 consecutive nights of strikes, according to CBS News reporting citing U.S. Central Command activity and U.S. officials.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Iran had halted retaliatory operations because the United States had stopped attacking; he also warned that fighting would expand if U.S. strikes resumed.

U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said the pause was intended to give diplomacy time, while the White House said President Trump still retained military options if Iran continued activity against shipping or U.S. allies.

sources.title: CBS News

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Neither side publicly set out binding terms, duration, or enforcement mechanisms for the pause, and the Pentagon did not explain why strikes stopped.

explore_lenses.label: What remains dangerous in the Strait of Hormuz?
explore_lenses.title: Shipping access remains the central dispute
explore_lenses.summary: The two governments still dispute who controls safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz, even as diplomacy focuses on reopening waterways. Recent Iranian interdictions indicate that the operational risk to commercial vessels has not ended with the attack pause.

claims.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on July 27 it turned back six vessels that attempted to use routes not approved by Iranian authorities, after warning shots were fired.

Iran has said the interim arrangement allows it to manage shipping through the strait and has objected to a U.S.-supported route nearer Oman's coast; the United States says the strait is open for transit.
The UN has warned that renewed U.S.-Iran strikes and disputes over Hormuz risk a wider war, and has called for restored navigational rights and freedoms.

explore_lenses.label: What diplomatic steps are confirmed next?
explore_lenses.title: Oman talks are active; a broader deal is unconfirmed
explore_lenses.summary: The clearest active channel is Iran-Oman discussion over waterways around Hormuz. Mediators are seeking a return to an interim agreement, but no date for direct U.S.-Iran talks or finalized ceasefire text has been publicly confirmed.

claims.text: An Iranian official told CBS News that discussions with Oman had been constructive and that talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz were moving in a positive direction; two regional sources said the diplomacy needed more time to reach a deal.

A regional official involved in mediation told the Associated Press that Pakistan, Qatar and others were working to restore the interim ceasefire, with a proposed compromise involving fewer restrictions on vessel transit managed by Iran.

Forecast: Waltz said the United States would assess the situation over the coming days, indicating that continuation of the pause depends on the administration's assessment rather than a publicly announced timetable.

related_stories.title: Severe Weather Claims Lives in China Amid Typhoon and Flooding
related_stories.summary: At least 10 people have died due to extreme weather conditions in China, including a powerful typhoon and flash flooding. The severe weather has prompted alerts across many regions, particularly affecting a tourist site in northwestern China. Nearly two dozen others have been reported injured as Typhoon Noul made landfall.

related_stories.title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
related_stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has responded to critics of the World Cup, accusing them of being 'consumed by hate' and spreading false narratives. In a strongly worded statement, he suggested that detractors should 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' instead of perpetuating negativity. Infantino defended the tournament as a celebration of unity, safety, and inclusion, dismissing concerns about corruption and disciplinary rulings.

related_stories.title: Severe Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations in France and Spain
related_stories.summary: Over 300,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in France and Spain due to severe wildfires that have been raging for several days. Fire crews are struggling to contain the unpredictable blazes, which have been exacerbated by an impending heatwave.
